prompt:
Design and implement the migration architecture for the estate in `fixtures/estate.json`. The destination is the single-site consolidated VMware Cloud Foundation design described by the inventory, and it must remain at the minimum supported management-domain host count. Migrate VMware Aria Operations, VMware Aria Automation, and VMware Aria Operations for Logs to VCF Operations, VCF Automation, and VCF Operations for Logs while carrying forward all compatible content and configuration.

Before finalizing the design, research Broadcom-published sources for the supported migration or upgrade path for each product, content compatibility and exclusions, sizing, placement, and end-of-general-support boundaries. Record each source consulted in `research.md` as one row of a Markdown table with the columns `Title`, `Publisher`, `Accessed`, `URL`, and `Design decision`. Use ISO `YYYY-MM-DD` access dates and HTTPS Broadcom URLs.

Produce `migration_plan.json` conforming to `schema/migration-plan.schema.json`. It must be an ordered, executable architecture rather than an explanatory report: name every entry in `source_products` with its version and target component; account exactly once for every inventoried content and configuration item as either carried forward or abandoned; state the transfer mode or disposition; include the applicable support boundary; make component placement, node count, sizing, capacity, availability, and vSAN failures-to-tolerate explicit; and give every migration step concrete actions and pass/fail gates.

Implement a standard-library-only Python package named `vcf_architecture` that exposes `build_plan(estate, compatibility)`. Its command-line interface must support `python3 -m vcf_architecture --inventory fixtures/estate.json --compatibility fixtures/compatibility_snapshot.json --output migration_plan.json` and write the same deterministic plan. Check in the generated `migration_plan.json`. The package must reject incompatible inputs rather than silently producing a partial plan. Preserve the supplied fixtures, schema, and tests. Run `python3 -B protected_tests/verify.py`.

network.reason: The task requires genuine research against currently reachable Broadcom migration, compatibility, sizing, placement, and lifecycle sources; deterministic acceptance verification itself is offline.
